claim: Iterating objectives is the key driver of progress in achieving a novel discovery with practical viability across multiple scientific design tasks.
falsifier: One could test whether varying the frequency or method of objective iteration changes the rate of practically viable discoveries in a held-out task.

conditions: Across five distinct scientific design tasks: antibiotic design, nanobody design, functional DNA sequence design, inorganic materials design, and chemical process optimization.
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the SAGA system and the five tasks reported; transferability to other tasks or systems is unestablished.

title: Iterating objectives during–Progress in achieving mechanism

claim: The satisfiability problem for Schönfinkel-Bernays expression segments (LSBS) is EXP-complete.
falsifier: One can verify that LSBS belongs to EXP by designing an exponential-time algorithm and prove EXP-hardness by reducing a known EXP-complete problem to LSBS.

conditions: under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions and reductions
exclusions: limited to the specific problem LSBS as defined in the source

title: The satisfiability problem–classification as EXP-complete theorem

claim: Directed Hamiltonicity in bipartite graphs and Undirected Hamiltonicity can be solved in O*(3^(n/2)) time on n-vertex graphs.
falsifier: Implement the algorithm and measure its running time on n-vertex directed bipartite and undirected instances, checking that it stays within O*(3^(n/2)).

conditions: directed bipartite graphs for Directed Hamiltonicity
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the formal theorem and its stated graph classes; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Hamiltonicity decision problems on–running time O* ) theorem
